records.region: Saskatchewan; southern Milligan Creek drainage, Foam Lake, and the Quill Lakes wetland complex
records.candidate_name_role: Supported river-component candidate; incomplete selected-system correspondence
records.material_pending_reason: The readable regional and project maps do not continuously establish the chosen long southern feeder from its opening through the intermediate bends and joins to the Foam Lake approach. The regional map and wetland/storage diagrams also do not adequately resolve the selected Foam Lake inlet-through-outlet passage and every lower wetland branch leading to Little Quill Lake. These are actual ordinary through-link gaps; missing present flow or structure-operation details are not being required.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The independent irrigation study names the Milligan Creek drainage, an existing creek at Helgasson Community Dam, and the downstream creek receiving Foam Lake releases. Its source cartography places the associated drainage southeast of Little Quill Lake. This supports a river-component candidate, without extending Milligan Creek across the terminal Quill lakes or completing the selected headward feeder correspondence.
records.completion_scope: All 33 stored parts of the one mainstem were considered. The Milligan component and receiving Quill lake complex are identified, and the terminal lake setting is supported. Source correspondence remains incomplete for the upstream and intervening creek/wetland passages.
records.supported_name_scope: Milligan Creek is a river-component name. Foam Lake, Little Quill Lake, Middle Quill Lake/Mud Lake and Big Quill Lake have separate lake identities. Helgason/Helgasson Community Dam is infrastructure context, not a substitute whole-system name.

scope_limits: Milligan Creek is supported as a component candidate, but the long selected southern opening and all creek/wetland links have not been established from readable primary cartography.
Regional drainage boundaries are not channel lines. Proposed in-stream and off-stream project symbols are not evidence that proposed works exist.
The source reports describe different lake-level epochs. Their ordinary connected-lake geography supports the selected receiving complex without establishing present water levels or exact banks.
This material-pending finding is not a completed name-scope hold and does not assert that the unnamed portions lack a local or official name.

records.region: Basse-Côte-Nord, Québec; Étamamiou corridor between the Olomane and Petit Mécatina river settings.
records.material_pending_reason: The northwestern opening-to-upper-junction link is absent from the CEHQ map. Station 075601’s opaque symbol and annotation conceal lower through-links and the actual final selected coastal endpoint. The author-route publication and river-profile prose do not close these exact ordinary-scale geography gaps, and the FQSA location map was unavailable.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The inspected CEHQ original supports Rivière Étamamiou along the depicted middle/lower corridor. The name is not imposed on every broadened water, lateral feeder or the omitted chosen opening. Whole-selected-system representative identity remains provisional.
records.completion_scope: All 47 selected parts were considered against the original regional map. Most of the depicted river corridor, broadened waters and joins are supported; the omitted opening and obscured lower/coastal connections remain material gaps.
records.supported_name_scope: The inspected CEHQ original supports Rivière Étamamiou along the depicted middle/lower corridor. The name is not imposed on every broadened water, lateral feeder or the omitted chosen opening. Whole-selected-system representative identity remains provisional.

scope_limits: The missing initial feeder prevents complete selected-system geographic correspondence.
The station symbol and data box conceal substantive lower links and the actual selected coastal endpoint; no exact-bank/current-flow/operating-state burden is imposed.
The pinned rendered endpoint differs from the source sea endpoint. Neither metadata point alone proves the coastal through-link.
Intermediate broadened and lake-like waters remain unnamed; no lake name is inferred from nearby prose or another itinerary.
The eight-river canoe itinerary includes portages and changes of drainage; its title is not a single natural river name or proof of continuous hydrography.
Formal registry status is unverified; no automatic/product application occurred.

records.region: Central coastal Labrador, interior west and southwest of the Big River–Adlavik Bay coast.
records.material_pending_reason: Readable independent corridor coverage is missing for the selected opening, interior lake/river through-links and joins, the northeastern river, and especially the materially northward stored terminal extension.
records.geographic_disambiguation: A named river is independently documented in the selected coastal region. Correspondence of the full selected interior path and actual rendered ending is not established; this remains a tentative Big River lead.
records.completion_scope: Bounded source pass remains incomplete for selected-path correspondence. One primary material-pending status covers all geographic gaps; source limitations are supporting detail.
records.supported_name_scope: A named river is independently documented in the selected coastal region. Correspondence of the full selected interior path and actual rendered ending is not established; this remains a tentative Big River lead.

scope_limits: Big River is a tentative regional identification, not a completed selected-system name or verified registry entry.
The initial selected feeder and intervening lakes may carry distinct names; none is inferred from model connectivity.
The stored northward terminal extension is explicitly unresolved rather than replaced with the river mouth.
The two failed sources supplied no substantive body or map evidence; discovery excerpts are not used as geographic proof.

records.material_pending_reason: Source-supported channel correspondence for the southwestern opening and its initial northward join. The western easterly transfer, including selected scattered-lagoon/depression entries and exits before Eduardo Castex. The selected through-passage at Monte Nievas and its eastward continuation beyond the thesis frame. The middle transfer and northeastern turn into the eastern southward corridor. Actual selected channel/reservoir correspondence across the northern and central cuenco approaches, rather than geographic coincidence with a planning footprint.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No representative river-system or selected-reach name is established. Sistema hídrico Eduardo Castex–Monte Nievas describes western regional context; Obra de los Daneses and its central cuenco describe the eastern terminal-planning setting. Neither is assigned as the name of the selected river.
records.completion_scope: All selected corridor intervals were considered. Western regional lagoon-system and eastern central-cuenco planning geography are established; opening, intervening channels and lagoon-to-lagoon connections remain incomplete.
records.supported_name_scope: No representative river-system or selected-reach name is established. Sistema hídrico Eduardo Castex–Monte Nievas describes western regional context; Obra de los Daneses and its central cuenco describe the eastern terminal-planning setting. Neither is assigned as the name of the selected river.

scope_limits: The selected trace may traverse diffuse runoff, intermittent depressions, lagoons and managed passages. Their complete connected sequence is not established by the inspected thematic maps.
A proposed reservoir footprint can establish regional terminal geography without proving every incoming selected channel.
Neither regional system labels nor the engineering scheme are established names for the entire modeled river.
No absence-of-name claim, formal registry match or Korean name is established.
The gaps concern ordinary geographic and channel correspondence, not exact banks, individual vertices, present water levels or operating details.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
